properties.statement:
A VERIFICATION HAS NOWHERE TO PUT ITS EVIDENCE, SO EVERY AUTHOR PUTS IT IN THE NAME. Median Verification `name` in this design is 79.5 WORDS.

MEASURED on the committed export, 2026-08-16: 160 Verifications — median name 79.5 words, 72 over 100 words, 17 over 300. The longest is 654 words. A `name` is what a list renders; these are reports.

⚠️ AND THE AUTHOR OF THE WORST OF IT TODAY WAS ME. Four of the six Verifications written in this session exceed 300 words, and `ver:a-claim-reads-back-with-its-age` at 435 words is the FIFTH LONGEST IN THE ENTIRE DESIGN. I was not working around a limitation I had noticed; I did not notice it. Every one of those nodes now costs its full length on every future read, in the field a list renders.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet, 2026-08-08 10:12, worker `w-02baf79f`, and their diagnosis is better than the symptom: `loop_status` is documented as "one cheap call", and it IS cheap to call and expensive to READ — their `verifications.attention[0].name` came back as a single ~450-word paragraph holding a full graded walk report, verdict, L0/L2/L3 legs, six measured field counts, refuted mechanisms and file:line citations. Their words: "That is excellent content and it is in the WRONG FIELD."

⭐ THE SHAPE OF IT, which is what makes it a defect rather than a style complaint: "workers write the full report into the `name` because there is no other durable place for it on the node — so this is A MISSING FIELD BEING PAID FOR IN EVERY FUTURE READ OF THAT NODE." The workaround is universal, undirected and invisible: nobody chose it, everybody does it, and it degrades the one call every worker is told to make routinely. A cheap call that returns prose nobody asked for is a call people stop making — the same signal-trained-to-be-ignored failure `req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes` was built to end, arriving through a different door.

THEIR TWO ASKS, recorded as filed:
(a) give Verification a `findings` / `report` property, so a walk's evidence has somewhere to live that is not its title;
(b) truncate `name` in `loop_status`'s rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the load-bearing question: whether (a) alone would change behaviour. A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is — the same trap `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` hit, where 112 nodes wrote an undeclared property because the declared route did not fit. The existing 160 names cannot be migrated automatically either: a property once written cannot be removed ([[fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed]]), so the best available repair is to write the evidence to the new field and SHORTEN the name, which duplicates rather than moves.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: whether (b) alone is enough. Truncating at the rollup makes the cheap call cheap again without asking anyone to change how they write — which is either the pragmatic fix or the one that lets the underlying hoard grow unchecked, and nobody has measured which.
